sets.title: Office Cafe Table
sets.contentHtml:
Eight colleagues, Arun, Bela, Chetan, Disha, Eshan, Fiza, Girish and Hina, sit around a circular table with eight equally spaced seats, all facing the centre. Each of them orders exactly one of four drinks: Tea, Coffee, Lassi or Juice, and each drink is ordered by exactly two of them.

Since everyone faces the centre, the person immediately to the left of anyone is the next person in the clockwise direction. 'X sits second to the left of Y' means that X is two seats away from Y in the clockwise direction.

The following is known:

  1. Bela sits second to the left of Arun.
  2. Chetan sits directly opposite Bela.
  3. Exactly one person sits between Disha and Girish.
  4. Hina sits next to Chetan.
  5. Eshan is not a neighbour of Arun and not a neighbour of Chetan.
  6. Eshan orders Coffee, and so does the person sitting directly opposite Eshan.
  7. Arun orders Lassi.
  8. Girish and Hina order the same drink.
  9. Fiza orders neither Tea nor Juice.
  10. Chetan does not order Juice.

sets.title: Studio Electives
sets.contentHtml:
All 90 first-year students of a design school had to register for at least one of three studio electives: Ceramics, Photography and Typography. A student could register for one, two or all three of them.

The following is known:

  1. Ceramics, Photography and Typography received 48, 45 and 38 registrations respectively.
  2. Exactly 25 students registered for exactly two electives.
  3. The number of students who registered for Photography only was three times the number who registered for both Ceramics and Typography but not Photography.
  4. Fewer students registered for Typography only than for Photography only.

sets.title: Rolling Cube Game
sets.contentHtml:
A cube has its faces numbered 1 to 6 such that the numbers on opposite faces add up to 7. It rests on a floor marked with square cells, each the size of a face, and can be rolled one cell at a time towards North (N), South (S), East (E) or West (W). Each roll tips the cube over one of its bottom edges:

  • Roll N: the top face turns to face North, the North face goes to the bottom, the bottom face turns to face South, and the South face comes to the top. The East and West faces do not change.
  • Roll S: the reverse of a roll N: the top face turns to face South, and the North face comes to the top.
  • Roll E: the top face turns to face East, the East face goes to the bottom, the bottom face turns to face West, and the West face comes to the top. The North and South faces do not change.
  • Roll W: the reverse of a roll E: the top face turns to face West, and the East face comes to the top.

Initially the cube shows 1 on top, 2 facing North and 3 facing East (so 6 is at the bottom, 5 faces South and 4 faces West).

Game. The cube starts, in this initial position, on the south-west corner cell of a 3 × 3 board and must reach the north-east corner cell in exactly four rolls, each of which is N or E (so exactly two rolls of each kind). The score of a route is the sum of the numbers on the top face after each of the four rolls; the initial top number is not counted.

questions.stemHtml: Who sits directly opposite Fiza?
questions.solutionHtml:
Seating. Number the seats 0 to 7 clockwise, with Arun in seat 0 (moving clockwise = moving to one's left). By conditions 1 and 2, Bela is in seat 2 and Chetan in seat 6. By condition 4, Hina is in seat 5 or 7. By condition 5, Eshan is not in seats 1, 7 (next to Arun) or 5 (next to Chetan), so Eshan is in seat 3 or 4.

If Eshan were in seat 4, the person opposite him would be Arun, who orders Lassi (condition 7), contradicting condition 6. So Eshan is in seat 3 and the person in seat 7 orders Coffee. That person is not Girish or Hina: they order the same drink, so both would need Coffee, giving three Coffee orders. If Fiza were in seat 7, Hina would be in seat 5 and seats 1 and 4 would be left for Disha and Girish, who must have exactly one person between them - impossible. Hence Disha is in seat 7. Girish must then be in seat 1 or 5; Hina needs seat 5 (seat 7 is taken), so Girish is in seat 1, Hina in seat 5 and Fiza in seat 4.

Drinks. Eshan and Disha order Coffee, and Arun orders Lassi. Fiza orders neither Tea nor Juice, and Coffee is used up, so Fiza orders Lassi. Chetan cannot order Juice, Coffee or Lassi, so he orders Tea. Girish and Hina order the same drink, which must be Tea or Juice; only one Tea is left, so both order Juice, and Bela orders the remaining Tea.

DrinkLassiJuiceTeaCoffeeLassiJuiceTeaCoffee

Fiza is in seat 4, and the seat opposite it is seat 0, which is Arun's. The answer is Arun.

questions.stemHtml: How many students registered for all three electives?
questions.solutionHtml:
Setting up. Let S, D and T be the numbers of students registered for exactly one, exactly two and all three electives. Then S + D + T = 90, and counting registrations, S + 2D + 3T = 48 + 45 + 38 = 131. Subtracting, D + 2T = 41; with D = 25, T = 8.

Let x = Ceramics and Photography only (not Typography), y = Ceramics and Typography only, z = Photography and Typography only, so x + y + z = 25.

Photography only = 45 - x - z - 8 = 37 - (25 - y) = 12 + y. By condition 3, 12 + y = 3y, so y = 6 and Photography only = 18. Then x + z = 19.

Typography only = 38 - y - z - 8 = 24 - z, and Ceramics only = 48 - x - y - 8 = 34 - x = 34 - (19 - z) = 15 + z.

Condition 4: 24 - z < 18, so z ≥ 7. Also x = 19 - z ≥ 0, so z ≤ 19. Every value of z from 7 to 19 gives a valid distribution.

The number registered for all three is 8.

questions.stemHtml: Suppose that in every ward, x% of the voters who voted for NP had instead voted for SD, where x is a whole number and all other votes stay unchanged. What is the smallest value of x for which SD would win at least three wards?
questions.solutionHtml:
Votes cast = registered voters × turnout, and each party's votes = votes cast × its share:

WardVotes castNPSDJMOthers
Amrapur52,00019,76017,68010,4004,160
Belgaon43,20012,96017,7129,5043,024
Chandni55,10019,28516,53017,0812,204
Devnagar56,00015,68018,48020,1601,680
Ekpur37,50015,7508,62510,1253,000

SD already wins Belgaon, and the shift only helps SD there. For each of the other wards, the condition for SD to win is:

  • Amrapur: SD needs 17,680 + 19,760x/100 > 19,760(1 - x/100), i.e., 395.2x > 2,080, x > 5.26. So x ≥ 6.
  • Chandni: SD must beat NP: 385.7x > 2,755, x > 7.14; and JM: 16,530 + 192.85x > 17,081, x > 2.86. So x ≥ 8.
  • Devnagar: SD must beat JM: 18,480 + 156.8x > 20,160, x > 10.7. So x ≥ 11.
  • Ekpur: SD must beat NP: 315x > 7,125, x > 22.6. So x ≥ 23.

Besides Belgaon, SD needs two more wards, and the two lowest thresholds are Amrapur (x ≥ 6) and Chandni (x ≥ 8). With x = 7, SD wins only Belgaon and Amrapur; with x = 8 it also wins Chandni (SD about 18,073 against NP about 17,742 and JM 17,081). The smallest x is 8.

None of the first five rolls restores the initial position, and the sixth does. The answer is 6.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following routes in the game ends with 6 on top and 2 facing North?
questions.solutionHtml:
Track the cube as (top, North, East); the other faces follow from 'opposite faces add to 7'. A roll N makes the new top = old South = 7 - old North and the new North = old top. A roll E makes the new top = old West = 7 - old East and the new East = old top. A roll S makes the new top = old North and the new North = 7 - old top.

  • E, E, N, N: final position (top 1, North 5, East 4)
  • E, N, N, E: final position (top 6, North 5, East 3)
  • N, N, E, E: final position (top 1, North 5, East 4)
  • N, E, E, N: final position (top 6, North 2, East 4)

Only N, E, E, N ends with 6 on top and 2 facing North (E, N, N, E ends with 6 on top but 5 facing North).
